correctness.rationale: For any connected finite graph the number of spanning trees in which a fixed vertex is a leaf is its graph degree times the spanning-tree count of the vertex-deleted graph (zero when disconnected). This bijection, together with the exactly computed deleted-matching and deleted-star Laplacian spectra and Kirchhoff tree counts, yields the two displayed closed forms. The matching sign is the strict Bernoulli inequality; the star sign is strict Jensen for two unequal positive bases with weighted mean one. The connectedness, r=1, n=2r and r=n-2 boundaries were checked explicitly. A standard-library exact Bareiss/minor checker independently passed 181 assertions, with small-graph brute enumeration. Finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The novel candidate is not the general ability to compute a UST leaf probability, which follows from known UST degree-field formulas, nor the classical graph-specific tree-count determinants. Rather, it is the explicitly evaluated pair of n,r-dependent leaf means and their strict, opposite signs for matching versus star deletions at equal removed-edge count, with the exact neutrality boundary at r=1. Searches of published mathematical literature and indexed findings with synonymous formulations did not retrieve an explicit equivalent theorem. Accessible full primary sources on generic UST degrees and moments were compared by implication, not merely by title. Historical-priority uncertainty persists: an earlier specialization or graph-extremal theorem might imply the comparison.

value.rationale: The sign of the change of mean leaf count under removing r edges is a natural robustness statistic in uniform random network trees. The two simplest ways for deleted edges to overlap, all disjoint versus all incident to one vertex, give strictly opposite effects for every admissible r>=2 despite identical host size and removed-edge counts, while r=1 is exactly neutral. This is an infinite-family structural boundary with explicit formulas, rather than a one-off graph counterexample or a small numeric perturbation. It does not claim extremality among all deletion patterns.
